issues.legal_issue: A party cannot raise on further appeal a contention concerning an adverse trial finding that it did not challenge in the intervening appeal.
material_facts: The trial court found that the transaction was a sale with an agreement to reconvey, rather than a mortgage by conditional sale.
The party against whom that finding was made did not challenge it when responding to the opposing parties’ appeal before the High Court.
The party attempted to renew the mortgage-by-conditional-sale contention in the further appeal.
issues.conclusion: The party could not agitate the mortgage-by-conditional-sale contention in the further appeal, and the contention failed.
issues.legal_principle: An adverse finding that was not challenged in the intervening appeal could not be reopened in the further appeal; the Court cited no earlier case for this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_from_a_judgment: A party brings an appeal from a judgment that followed an earlier appeal.
predicates.adverse_finding_not_challenged_in_interv: A party does not challenge an adverse finding when responding to the opposing side’s intervening appeal.
predicates.previously_unchallenged_contention_canno: The party is not permitted to raise again the contention that depended on the unchallenged finding.

issues.definition: When a party appeals after leaving an adverse finding unchallenged in an intervening appeal, the party cannot raise again a contention based on that finding.

issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff seeking specific performance must plead the agreement relied on, a specific request that it be performed, and continuing readiness and willingness to perform the plaintiff’s part.
material_facts: The suit sought specific performance of an agreement to reconvey property.
The plaintiff alleged that the documents recording the transactions were sham and unsupported by consideration.

The trial court found that the documents were genuine and operative, that consideration had been paid, and that possession and title had passed; the plaintiff did not challenge those findings in the High Court.
The plaint did not plead that the plaintiff had specifically requested performance of the agreement or that the plaintiff had been and remained ready and willing to perform his part.
issues.conclusion: The plaint did not contain the pleadings required for specific performance, so the plaintiff was not entitled to that relief.
issues.legal_principle: A suit for specific performance must conform to Forms 47 and 48 in the First Schedule to the Code of Civil Procedure: the plaintiff must set out the agreement, plead a specific application to the defendant to perform it and the defendant’s failure to do so, and plead that the plaintiff has been and remains ready and willing to perform. The Court applied Ouseph Varghese v. Joseph Aley and relied on its statement of the rule, including its reference to Pt. Prem Rai v. The D.L.F. Housing and Construction (Private) Ltd.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A plaintiff brings a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement.
predicates.pleaded_specific_request_for_performance: The plaintiff pleads that the plaintiff specifically asked the defendant to perform the agreement and that the defendant did not do so.
predicates.pleaded_continuing_readiness_and_willing: The plaintiff pleads readiness and willingness to perform the plaintiff’s part, both previously and at present.
predicates.specific_performance_decree_unavailable: The plaintiff cannot obtain a decree for specific performance.

issues.definition: In a suit for specific performance, if the plaintiff has not pleaded either a specific request for performance or continuing readiness and willingness, a decree for specific performance is unavailable.
